subject: Seat-to-consumption pricing blend — concession scenarios and integration fee split
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@edgecorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeCorp Procurement <procurement@edgecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up — packaging asks and parity vs CloudScale

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. I attached our RFP summary and a short usage extract so you have context (EdgeCorp_RFP_Q3.pdf). We're evaluating a move away from CloudScale and want to see if Redwood can match commercial terms while addressing integration friction. A few specific asks: 

- We want a hybrid commercial structure: baseline committed seats (for steady-state) + burst consumption for spiky workloads. What's your recommended seat-to-consumption breakpoints?
- How do you price overage vs committed consumption?
- We expect an integration/engineering workstream (~6–8 weeks). Would Redwood split integration fees or offer onboarding credits?
- Any constraints around caching/KV warm strategies that affect cost parity?
- Can you provide a 12-month blended forecast and a pilot rate for proof of concept?

We need a competitive price-equivalent proposal (CloudScale is offering an aggressive fixed-seat uplift with no egress credits). If you can send a couple of scenario sketches (committed/consumption blends + indicative rates) before Friday, that would help procurement.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeCorp

Attachments: EdgeCorp_RFP_Q3.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@edgecorp.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — packaging asks and parity vs CloudScale

Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks and the usage extract. I reviewed the RFP and sketched three commercially distinct scenarios — attached as redwood_scenarios_v2.xlsx. High level: 

Option A — Seat-first: Conservative committed seats that mirror CloudScale (min operational risk). Minimal onboarding credit. Overages charged at a higher rate to protect run rate. Good if EdgeCorp wants predictability.

Option B — Blended baseline + burst (our recommended pilot): Lower committed seats, capped burst consumption at a blended overage rate (lower than pure overage). Includes a pilot credit of $25k and 50% integration-fee split if EdgeCorp commits to a 12-month term. This preserves unit economics for us while reducing upfront customer lift.

Option C — Consumption-led: Minimal seats, prepay consumption bucket with volume discount tiers and a one-time integration discount in lieu of credits. Best for companies willing to accept variability for lower unit costs.

Key constraints/notes: 
- Dedicated KV-cache pinning (for low-latency workloads) changes how we treat cache warm costs — can't fully credit that back.
- Egress concessions are possible but limited; we can include one-time egress credits tied to migration data transfer.
- Pricing sensitivity: to match CloudScale parity we'll need a term commitment and at least a 12-month baseline in either A or B.

Can you confirm which scenario you'd like us to flesh out into a one-page MAP (mutual action plan)? If Option B looks closest I can run our legal/commercial playbook and circulate a MAP_draft.docx plus a short DocuSign LOI link.

I'll also loop Connor for engineering input and Vanessa for any SLA/technical concession notes.

Thanks —
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_scenarios_v2.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@edgecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — packaging asks and parity vs CloudScale

Marcus/Connor —

Quick technical read on the three scenarios Marcus sketched: 

- Option B is the most implementable with minimal operational debt. For the blended overage to hold, we need clear SLA triggers for burst autoscaling to avoid sustained backfills that blow the blended math. Recommend: burst = 30% of peak baseline for pilot, auto-burst throttle after 60s sustained spike.
- KV cache warm: if EdgeCorp expects warm-starts at scale during cutover we will need to include a migration warm-cache window and associated EC2/GPU time. That cost should sit in the integration bucket — not counted against credits. 
- Integration fee split: 50/50 is acceptable for a 12-month commitment and a committed-seat minimum of 60% of current peak usage. If procurement pushes lower, we reduce the integration split and increase pilot credits.

I'll prepare a brief tech appendix for the MAP with recommended throttles, warm-cache runbook, and required instrumentation. Connor — can you provide a short estimate for the warm-cache run (hours / GPU-days) so we can quantify the migration credit?

Vanessa
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@edgecorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeCorp Procurement <procurement@edgecorp.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — packaging asks and parity vs CloudScale

Marcus/Vanessa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and helpful options. After internal review, EdgeCorp prefers Option B as a balance between predictability and cost savings. Two asks to finalize the pilot: 

1) Can you put the MAP_draft.docx in one-pager form and include the following bullets: committed seats, blended burst cap, pilot credit amount ($25k), 50% integration-fee split, and 12-month minimum term.
2) Please quantify the warm-cache run estimate (Connor) and mark that as eligible for migration credit, separate from the pilot credit.

If we can get the one-pager and a short LOI (DocuSign) by EOD Wednesday we can route to our procurement and legal teams for redlines. CloudScale is pushing a hard deadline for their counteroffer, so timeboxed cadence matters.

Elena
Head of Platform Engineering — EdgeCorp

Attachments: none
